title: Knesset advances bill to strip rights from MKs who won't call Hamas terror group
description: The Knesset on Wednesday approved in a preliminary reading a bill that would strip lawmakers who refuse to recognize Hamas as a terrorist organization of their rights as MKs, the parliament said. The amendment to Basic Law: the Knesset, sponsored by MK Ofir Katz (Likud), passed 48-0, sending it to the Arrangements Committee, which will decide where it is deliberated. "This law states that a Member of the Knesset who does not recognize Hamas as a terrorist organization will not receive a salary from the State of Israel," Katz said. "It is absurd that we even need to legislate such a law." Opposition MKs, including Arab lawmakers, walked out before the vote, leaving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition alone in the plenum, Hebrew media reported. The Yashar party, led by Gadi Eisenkot, told Channel 14 it would not take part in "Likud's shows" and called every Likud proposal on Wednesday "embarrassing trolling." On Tuesday, the Eisenkot-led bloc that is seeking to replace Netanyahu elected Yashar MK Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker over Katz, with the backing of the Arab Joint List and Ra'am parties.

The expanded service will operate from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. to 7 p.m., connecting the capital with Ben-Gurion International Airport, Tel Aviv, Herzliya and Netanya. description: Otzma Yehudit lawmaker Yitzhak Kroizer told JNS on Wednesday that the election of Matan Kahana (Yashar) as Knesset speaker this week was a "badge of shame," because it relied on votes from the Arab Ra'am and Joint List parties. Kroizer pointed out that MKs from both parties walked out of the plenum during the singing of "Hatikvah," Israel's national anthem, as part of the Knesset's swearing-in ceremony last week. "It is a slap in the face to the fallen soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces, the victims of terror, and those currently serving in the IDF," he said, adding that lawmakers who "glorify 'martyrs'" and refuse to condemn the Hamas terror group are now "playing a decisive role" in the Knesset. Kroizer called Kahana, a former Israeli Air Force pilot who served as religious services minister under then-Prime Minister Naftali Bennett in 2021 and 2022, "a worthy individual who has contributed greatly to the state." However, the speaker was elected with the votes of "Tibi, Abbas, and their associates," Kroizer said. He noted the Arab lawmakers had dedicated their gains in the Oct. 27 election to "their 'brothers,' the Nukhba terrorists in Gaza." "This badge of shame will remain with him forever," Kroizer said. "It must be clear to the public that these parties do not seek the well-being of Israel's citizens; rather, time and again, they align themselves with those who seek our destruction," he added. "We will challenge this using parliamentary and public tools, fight against these decisions, and remind the public of the gap between pre-election promises and actions taken in the Knesset."

title: Knesset votes to extend longstanding state of emergency
description: Knesset lawmakers voted 8-1 on Wednesday to extend Israel's national state of emergency until March 18, 2027, the parliament said. The plenum approved a recommendation by the temporary Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, following a government request. The declaration is usually renewed for a year, but the temporary committee formed after the Oct. 27 Knesset election can only approve four-month extensions, Hebrew media reported. The declaration has been in effect since the Jewish state's founding in 1948, when the Provisional State Council issued it. It lets the government enact emergency regulations that can override Knesset legislation, subject to legal limits. It also keeps certain laws and orders that depend on the emergency in force.

title: A century of hope: How global medical breakthroughs shape the future of healthcare
description: Imagine being told you will never walk again, and then, through sheer resilience and world-class care, taking your very first steps. Imagine waiting for a lifesaving medical treatment that does not yet exist, only to benefit from a pioneering discovery that completely rewrites your future. Every day at Hadassah hospitals in Jerusalem, these inspiring stories unfold. Behind every outcome is a dedicated team of physicians, researchers and innovators pushing the boundaries of medicine. From complex, groundbreaking surgeries to vital advances in treatments for diseases affecting people across the globe, the impact extends far beyond borders. Hadassah, The Women’s Zionist Organization of America , powers the work of the hospitals through the collective strength of 300,000 members, Associates and supporters. It is a life-changing force for those who heal and for those who help make that healing possible. An international impact driven by research and care The scale of care delivered at Hadassah hospitals is immense. Each year, the organization serves more than 1 million patients, touching the lives of 1 in 10 Israelis. In 2025 alone, Hadassah hospitals welcomed 19,007 newborns into the world; performed 51,882 surgeries with precision care; launched nearly 2,000 clinical trials; and were awarded 25 new patents. The cutting-edge care is transformational. Take the story of Jonathan, a father of three who suffered severe, life-threatening trauma following a major highway accident. Transferred directly to the Level 1 trauma center at Hadassah Hospital Ein Kerem, his survival depended on an intricate, multistage surgical intervention led by an interdisciplinary team. Today, he is back home with his family, which is a testament to the hospital’s world-renowned emergency response and medical ingenuity. Whether pioneering research in cancer, ALS, Alzheimer’s disease or trauma medicine, Hadassah hospitals serve as a crucial bridge to peace, modeling a shared society through interfaith cooperation in daily clinical care and international medical collaboration. When terror, natural disasters or healthcare crises strike, Hadassah is on the frontlines. In the United States, Hadassah does more than support the compassionate care and research at its hospitals; it unites generations of women and families in purpose. Through dedicated support for Youth Aliyah Villages , Hadassah provides shelter, education, counseling, compassion and essential life skills to vulnerable teens and pre-teens in Israel, helping over 300,000 graduates build bright futures since 1934. At a time when the Jewish state and the global Jewish community face extraordinary challenges, Hadassah remains nonpartisan, advocating for women’s health equity; speaking out against hate and antisemitism; and championing a strong and secure Israel. Driven by a movement of women changemakers, the organization gives individuals the tools to lead, connect and create impact. At Hadassah, we believe that each of us has the potential to make a difference. How to get involved Healing the world takes action. There are ways to make an enduring impact: •       Become a member : Join a national network of nearly 300,000 women and advocates standing together for Israel and women's health. •       Support lifesaving research : Donate to fund pioneering medical research and state-of-the-art facilities and equipment at Hadassah hospitals. •       Advocate for change : Participate in national campaigns fighting antisemitism and anti-Zionism and advancing women’s health. Learn how you can be part of this legacy of hope and healing by exploring Our Impact . Visit: Hadassah.org .

The agreement with the heirs of publisher Samuel Fischer concerned the “Châtaigniers en fleurs” (“Chestnut Trees in Blossom”), which is to be auctioned in New York on Wednesday and whose worth was estimated at $180 million. The terms of the agreement were not disclosed. The U.S.-based heirs, who had asked Sotheby’s to freeze the sale, said the 1890 work was sold in Amsterdam in 1936 because of financial losses their family’s publishing company suffered under Nazi rule. The Netherlands was not then under Nazi control, but the heirs argue that persecution in Germany forced the sale.

title: New Sderot tennis center supports children affected by Oct. 7 attacks
description: A new tennis and education center opened in Sderot last week, offering sports, educational and resilience programs for children affected by the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks. The Israel Tennis & Education Centers (ITEC) facility aims to provide a supportive environment for children and families in the Gaza Envelope. The center will offer a tennis-based mental health program for children coping with trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Specially trained coaches and staff will lead sessions in schools across the region to help children build confidence, resilience and social connections. The facility includes four tennis courts, a practice area, a studio, a reinforced safe room and four protective shelters. “This center offers them far more than tennis. It gives them a safe place to come together, make friends and discover what they are capable of,” Sderot Mayor Alon Davidi said at the opening ceremony. “The children of Sderot and the Gaza Envelope have been through so much, and it is our responsibility to make sure every child knows they have a future here.”

description: The first female recruits in an Israel Defense Forces trial integrating women into Armored Corps combat roles will enlist this week, the military said on Tuesday. Physical fitness training will be adapted to safeguard their fitness and health, and they will complete a preparatory combat fitness course. Men and women will not serve together in the same tank crews during training or operations. The IDF said the initiative reflects an operational need to expand its ranks and strengthen its combat forces.

title: British taxpayer funds sent to Palestinian museum accused of glorifying terrorists
description: British taxpayers’ money has helped fund a Palestinian museum accused of glorifying terrorists responsible for murdering Israeli civilians, prompting the Charity Commission, which oversees charities in England and Wales, to open a regulatory compliance case, UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI) said this week. UKLFI, a pro-Israel legal group, urged the commission to investigate after finding that the Palestinian Museum in Birzeit in Samaria portrays murderers and terrorist leaders as heroes, martyrs and freedom fighters. In a letter to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy, UKLFI called for an examination of whether British public money had been used to conserve or digitize material celebrating terrorists. Among the items highlighted in a UKLFI report: a poster celebrating Dalal al-Mughrabi, who led the 1978 Coastal Road massacre in which 38 Israeli civilians, including 13 children, were killed; a poster calling Abu Jihad, who masterminded that massacre, “the leading hero”; a leaflet commemorating Yahya Ayyash, a Hamas bomb-maker responsible for attacks that killed more than 80 Israelis. The museum has received support through a U.K. charity, the Welfare Association (also known as Taawon UK), the British Library and the British Council’s Cultural Protection Fund (CPF), which awarded £152,208 (about $200,000) in 2019 to a project involving the Palestinian Museum.

description: Israel is tied with Japan for second place among 20 countries surveyed for the share of startups developing physical artificial intelligence, according to an Amazon Web Services (AWS) study published in October and reported by CTech on Monday. The study found that 21% of Israeli startups are active in the field, behind Germany at 24% but ahead of the United States at 20%. Physical AI enables machines such as robots, drones and autonomous vehicles to perceive and interact with their surroundings. The study surveyed 4,420 startups, including 663 developing physical AI technology. Despite the sector's growth, 70% of developers worldwide said slow customer adoption was limiting their expansion.

In its expression of concern, the ministry reposted a statement by Al-Haq in which the group claimed that its general director, Shawan Jabarin, had been "banned from travelling outside Palestine by Israel" and called on "third states" to "intervene." Included in the reposted statement were the hashtags “#EndIsraeliImpunity" and "#EndIsraeliApartheid.” Al-Haq was designated as a terrorist group by Israel in 2021, and was sanctioned by the United States the following year. The Ramallah-based group, established in 1979, operates as an arm of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), according to Israel. Israel alleges that Al-Haq received substantial funding from European governments and international organizations as part of a PFLP network. Al-Haq denies the allegations.

title: Norwegian university suspends professor over Holocaust remarks
description: A Norwegian university on Monday said it suspended a history professor from teaching after an Austrian newspaper reported that he had disputed the existence of Nazi extermination camps. Stephan Sander-Faes, a professor at the University of Bergen in Norway, wrote that there were “no dedicated ‘annihilation’ or ‘death camps,'” Der Standard reported earlier this month, citing a blog post he published under a pseudonym while employed at the university. The paper's article did not say when exactly Sander-Faes had allegedly disputed the existence of Nazi death camps. He accused the paper of taking his comments out of context. The suspension takes immediate effect and will last until at least the end of the spring semester in 2027, university rector Margareth Hagen told Norwegian broadcaster NRK . The newspaper also reported that he had replied “Exactly” to a comment on social media suggesting fewer than 6 million Jews died in the Holocaust. I commend the swift action taken by the rector of the University of Bergen to suspend the professor. As survivors fade away, we must be increasingly vigilant and ensure zero tolerance for Holocaust denial and distortion. https://t.co/I3X4UZKh6F https://t.co/QjDnea2u24 pic.twitter.com/ju1wsylRWr — Eytan Halon (@eytanhalon) November 16, 2026 Israel’s chargé d’affaires in Norway, Eytan Halon, welcomed the suspension. “As survivors fade away, we must be increasingly vigilant and ensure zero tolerance for Holocaust denial and distortion,” he wrote on X. Sander-Faes apologized to Holocaust survivors, NRK reported. "The Holocaust is an established historical fact, and I do not deny any of the crimes committed by the Nazi regime. Any claim to the contrary is absurd and without evidence," NRK quoted him as saying. "I deeply regret the confusion, distress and pain my texts have caused and wish to offer an unreserved apology to Holocaust survivors and all others who were affected by the crimes of Nazism."

title: University of Haifa gets $8.8 million grant to establish Israel’s first national suicide-care training center
description: The University of Haifa has established Israel’s first national center dedicated to suicide care training, supported by an $8.8 million, five-year grant from Overlake Fund. The pioneering initiative aims to transform suicide prevention and care across Israel, equipping thousands of professionals with the skills and resources to support people in crisis, establishing national standards of care and helping build a stronger, more coordinated mental-health response at a time of unprecedented need. The National Training Center for Suicide Care comes amid growing concerns about the long-term psychological impact of the Hamas-led terrorist attacks in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, and the ensuing war. Research conducted by University of Haifa professor Yossi Levi-Belz and colleagues at Columbia University found that probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) among Israeli adults nearly doubled in the month following the attacks, rising from 16.2% to 29.8%. Rates of probable depression increased from 31.3% to 44.8%, while probable anxiety rose from 24.9% to 42.7%. Although Israel’s suicide rate has not increased, subsequent research has identified rising suicidal thoughts among certain high-risk populations, particularly reserve-duty combatants, underscoring the urgent need to strengthen the country’s suicide prevention and treatment infrastructure. Over its first five years, the center aims to train approximately 4,500 mental-health professionals and frontline personnel, while reaching an additional 12,000 community members through programs designed to help identify individuals at risk and connect them with appropriate care. “Israel is facing a profound mental health challenge, and the years ahead will be critical," said professor Yossi Levi-Belz, Founding Academic Director of the National Training Center for Suicide Care and Head of the University of Haifa’s Lior Tsfaty Center for Suicide and Mental Pain Studies. "We have an opportunity and a responsibility to fundamentally transform how suicide care is understood, taught, and delivered across the country. By equipping professionals with the right skills, establishing consistent standards, and strengthening coordination across our healthcare system, we can ensure that more people receive the support they need at their most vulnerable moments and ultimately help save lives.” At the heart of the center will be an advanced simulation facility incorporating artificial intelligence, virtual reality and realistic clinical scenarios. Using AI-powered simulators developed and tested by University of Haifa researchers, mental-health professionals will be able to practice conversations with simulated patients experiencing suicidal crises, receiving immediate feedback to strengthen their assessment and intervention skills. The technology will be complemented by virtual-reality scenarios and sessions involving professional actors portraying patients, while a cloud-based platform will extend training opportunities to professionals across Israel. The approach builds on University of Haifa research, including a 2025 study published in The Journal of Clinical Psychiatry that found significant improvements in mental-health professionals’ confidence in assessing suicide risk after training with an AI-powered simulator. Beyond its technological innovations, the center will work to address longstanding gaps in Israel’s mental-health system, including shortages of specially trained professionals, inconsistent clinical practices, and inadequate coordination between healthcare and community services. “We are deeply grateful to Overlake Fund for its partnership in establishing the National Training Center for Suicide Care,” said University of Haifa president Gur Alroey. “This gift reflects a shared commitment to one of the most urgent challenges facing Israeli society, and it marks the growing role of the University of Haifa in shaping Israel’s future. Together, we are building the professional expertise needed to strengthen suicide prevention and improve care for people at risk nationwide.” The center’s programs will target psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, physicians, nurses, and other frontline professionals, with an initial focus on northern and southern Israel. The center will also collaborate with national institutions, including the Ministry of Health’s Suicide Prevention Unit, the Ministry of Defense Rehabilitation Division, the IDF Mental Health Department and Israel’s national health funds. Community-based training will further equip teachers, youth leaders and other individuals who frequently encounter people in distress with the skills to recognize warning signs and connect those at risk with appropriate support. Building on the University of Haifa’s established expertise in suicide prevention and mental health research, the center will develop approximately 80 training programs and partnerships with 15 major organizations over its first five years. Its activities will be introduced in phases, with the broader goal of establishing a coordinated national framework for suicide care that strengthens professional training, improves access to specialized support and helps save lives.

Spanberger’s administration told The Washington Post that it did not believe the program would benefit public-school students and that Virginia would not participate this year. Her Republican predecessor, Glenn Youngkin, had initiated enrollment. Starting in 2027, the program will provide a federal tax credit of up to $1,700 for qualifying donations to scholarship-granting organizations. Eyal Zamir, the Supreme Court and Rabbi Dov Lando, a leading Haredi rabbi. "It will not mean conscription for everyone, but it will be the fairest law," he said. description: The Israeli Defense Ministry's director general, Maj. Gen. (res.) Amir Baram, said on Monday that "the next surprises on the battlefield" will come from Israel's defense-tech sector. "We are investing hundreds of millions of shekels in Israeli defense tech," Baram said during a visit to Kela Technologies, a startup that integrates technologies such as AI into military systems. The company was founded after the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks. During the visit, Baram was shown detection, warning, strike and interception systems that Kela developed with the ministry's Directorate of Defense Research and Development. Israel "must continue to increase investment" in defense-tech firms, Baram said, adding that "the economic dividend will be no less significant than the security one." Kela CEO Alon Dror said every shekel from the ministry is leveraged "dozens of times over" into research and development. "We are building manufacturing independence for Israel," he said. The visit was part of a series of visits Baram has made to Israeli defense-tech companies, the ministry said.

title: Israel’s inflation falls to 5-year low as housing prices decline
description: Israel’s annual inflation rate fell to 1.1% in October from 1.6% in September, its lowest level in more than five years, as the Consumer Price Index unexpectedly declined by 0.1%, according to figures released on Sunday by the Central Bureau of Statistics. Economists had forecast a monthly increase of as much as 0.5%. Fresh fruit prices fell by 2.8% and transportation costs declined by 1.4%, while clothing and footwear prices rose by 4.1%. Housing prices also continued to fall, declining by 0.2% in August-September compared with the previous two-month period and by 1.5% from a year earlier. New apartment prices fell by 0.7% over the same two months and by 0.2% from a year earlier. The Bank of Israel held its benchmark interest rate at 3.25% in late October, following three consecutive rate cuts.

description: Israeli security forces arrested a resident of northern Israel who allegedly photographed strategic sites, military bases and police stations on behalf of Iranian intelligence operatives, the Israel Police and the Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet) said in a joint statement on Sunday. The suspect—identified as Wissam Ghaleb Saleh Awad, an Israeli citizen from Mazra'a, near Nahariya—was arrested after investigators opened a probe last month and raided his home. According to the statement, Awad contacted Iranian agents himself through Telegram. He allegedly offered his services for ideological reasons, "out of a desire to carry out an act of revenge," and took no money. He also expressed identification with terrorist organizations, including Iranian-backed Lebanese Hezbollah, the statement said. He allegedly passed footage and location coordinates to his handlers "for future use." title: Israeli DM warns against bringing Ra'am into next government
description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz (Likud) warned on Sunday of "grave consequences" for the Jewish state's security if opposition parties succeed in bringing the United Arab List (Ra'am) into a new government. In a Hebrew-language statement, Katz cited Egypt's recent move to permanently outlaw the Muslim Brotherhood. Ra'am maintains close ties to the Muslim Brotherhood and Hamas. The United States welcomed Cairo's decision, as did many Arab states, the defense minister noted. "Only here in Israel are there those who are working, even after the events of Oct. 7, [2023,] to bring Hamas's sister movement into the coalition and the government," he said. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas "is not even willing to define Hamas as a terrorist organization," said Katz. "Those willing to topple the president of the largest and strongest Arab state in the name of extreme Islamist ideology will not hesitate to slaughter the Jewish state if given the chance," he added. He was referring to what he described as the Muslim Brotherhood's plans to stir up a revolution against Egyptian President Fattah Abdel el-Sisi. title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising memorial vandalized with Ukrainian nationalist graffiti
description: The memorial honoring fighters of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, as well as a nearby Polish military monument, were defaced with red graffiti praising a Ukrainian nationalist militia.
